observation.visible_scene: A calm, mirror-like water surface reflecting a bright blue sky filled with white cumulus clouds and a thin high wispy cloud streak. The horizon sits near the vertical center; the lower half shows the near-perfect reflection of the clouds. A faint yellowish-green blurred patch is visible underwater at the bottom-center of the frame.
visible_changes: The thin high wispy cloud near the top center drifts slowly leftward across the segment (its position shifts from roughly center-top in the early frames toward the upper-left by the last frame), while the main puffy cumulus clouds remain essentially fixed in frame position, indicating cloud motion rather than a camera pan.

A small dark speck (a tiny object on the water surface) appears on the right side of the water around the middle of the segment (t≈0.47s) and persists in roughly the same location through the final frame.
The underwater yellowish-green blur at the bottom stays largely in place with only minor shape/position fluctuation; the cloud reflections track the (nearly stationary) clouds above.
Overall the scene is near-static: no object enters or exits the main clouds, and the water surface shows no visible ripples or waves during the excerpt.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the high thin cloud continues drifting or the dark speck moves further/leaves after the crop ends is not shown.
The cause of the dark speck's appearance (e.g., a bird, leaf, or insect landing) is not visible within the segment.
What the yellowish-green underwater patch is, and whether it is moving, cannot be determined from these frames.
uncertain_details: Camera motion is uncertain but appears minimal/static because the cumulus clouds and horizon do not translate appreciably; the leftward shift is best attributed to the thin cloud itself.
The dark speck's identity and whether it is a reflection or a surface object cannot be confirmed.
The exact direction/speed of the thin cloud drift is small and may be partly rendering/looping artifact rather than true motion.
